narration: Dollar stores are now more common than McDonald's and Starbucks combined. Fifty-four million Americans shop them every week to save money. But here's the wild part — they're secretly one of the most expensive stores in America.
visual: Dollar store storefront SVG with red '$1.25' signs in every window. Row of person silhouettes walking through the door. Badge at top reads '36,000 LOCATIONS'. Text overlay below: '54 MILLION SHOPPERS/WEEK ALL THINKING THEY'RE SAVING'.

narration: That bottle of detergent costs $1.25 and feels like a steal. But dollar store detergent runs twenty-two cents per ounce. Costco runs six cents per ounce. You're paying nearly four times as much per wash.
visual: Two laundry detergent bottles side by side. Left: small dollar store bottle labeled '$1.25 — 22¢ per oz'. Right: large bulk bottle labeled '$11.09 — 6¢ per oz'. Animated horizontal bar chart below shows the per-oz comparison. '4x MORE EXPENSIVE' label springs in.

narration: Dollar stores deliberately sell tiny packages — not to help you, but to hide the real price. Your brain sees $1.25 and stops doing math. Researchers call this unit-price blindness, and retailers engineer it on purpose.
visual: Product package with huge '$1.25' price and tiny '5.7 oz' text almost invisible. Arrow pointing to simple SVG brain graphic. A red blindfold bar overlays the brain. Text box reveals: 'SMALL PACKAGES = HIDDEN COST — DELIBERATE. ENGINEERED.'

narration: Here's the part that makes it worse. Seventy-three percent of dollar stores cluster in lower-income neighborhoods where residents have fewer grocery alternatives. The people with the least money pay the highest per-unit prices.
visual: City grid map. Red dollar-sign dots appear progressively, clustering in a highlighted lower-income zone. A few scattered dots elsewhere. Legend and text: '73% IN LOW-INCOME AREAS — FEWEST ALTERNATIVES. HIGHEST PRICES.'

narration: If you spend sixty dollars a month on household basics at a dollar store, you're overpaying by about $1,400 a year versus buying equivalent products in larger sizes. Over a working life, that's $140,000.
visual: Receipt/math breakdown: '$60/mo dollar store spend' vs '$43/mo bulk equivalent'. Animated counter counts up to $1,400 annual overpayment, then $140,000 lifetime total. Red highlighted total box with '40-YEAR DRAIN' label.

narration: Next time you pick up that $1.25 item, flip the package and check the ounces. Unit price is the number that actually matters. Follow for more money traps dressed up as savings.
visual: Package front showing big '$1.25' fades out. Package flips to reveal unit price: '22¢/oz — YOU PAY 267% MORE'. Piggy bank SVG appears. CTA text: 'UNIT PRICE = REAL PRICE — FOLLOW FOR MORE MONEY TRAPS'.
